name: Today Is the Day
label: AmRep
lede: Steve Austin taught himself to record on a Fostex four-track at twelve, and he has run Today Is the Day his own way since 1992. Two future Mastodon members passed through in the middle.

eras.title: A Nashville demo lands at AmRep
eras.text: Steve Austin and Brad Elrod start in Nashville, add a bassist and self-finance a tape that gets them onto Amphetamine Reptile Records. Two albums follow in two years.

years.h: Steve Austin and Brad Elrod start Today Is the Day in Nashville
years.p: They had played together in Alien in the Land of Our Birth. Mike Herrell joins on bass, and the self-financed EP How to Win Friends and Influence People is the first release.

years.h: A homemade tape gets Amphetamine Reptile's attention
years.p: Wikipedia says the self-released tape got them a deal with [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s Amphetamine Reptile Records, the Minneapolis label that also had [[Unsane|db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b]] and [[Cows|d4b064a0-5567-4930-a359-16fadfa7941b]].

years.h: Noise rock leans toward metal on Supernova
years.p: Twelve songs in 53 minutes, recorded at AmRep's own studio in Minneapolis with Austin and Tim Mac producing. AllMusic's Patrick Kennedy called it a "landmark recording."
years.xp:
Austin has said the opening song "Adult World" came from downtown Nashville in the early nineties, which felt seedy and dangerous, and from a strip club of the same name (CLRVYNT interview).

Last Rites wrote that it laid groundwork for a wave of spastic metal bands. Deadguy drummer Dave Rosenberg has named it among his all-time favorites.

years.h: Willpower is cut in Detroit right after Austin's father is killed
years.p: Recorded at White Room Studios, per Wikipedia. The album runs 29 minutes, opens with a spoken clip from Goodfellas and works "Amazing Grace" into "Promised Land."
years.xp:
Steve Austin's father was killed in a car crash just before the sessions (Wikipedia).

It is the only Today Is the Day album made with the same lineup as its predecessor: Austin, Elrod and Herrell.

Austin told Antichrist Magazine he realized around Willpower that the music hit listeners hard because he kept everything real, however painful.

years.h: AmRep's Clusterfuck '94 puts the band beside Chokebore and Guzzard
years.p: AmRep put the band on one record with Chokebore and Guzzard.

eras.title: Austin runs short of people and money
eras.text: The self-titled record is the last AmRep album, with Elrod and a keyboardist. By the next one Austin is broke, living in his studio warehouse and on a metal label.

years.h: The last AmRep album adds a keyboardist
years.p: Recorded at Austin's own Austin Enterprise studio in Nashville, with Elrod on drums and Scott Wexton on synthesizer and sampler, his only studio album with the band.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Austin, Elrod and Wexton on this record and gives no reason for the bass and keyboard changes that followed.

A remastered SuperNova edition in 2008 added two tracks first released on AmRep's Clusterfuck compilations.

years.h: Temple of the Morning Star moves the band from AmRep to Relapse
years.p: Recorded in July 1997 at Austin Enterprise with Mike Hyde on drums and Chris Reeser on bass. Liner notes say Austin was very poor and living in an abandoned warehouse.
years.xp:
Austin told Vice the space was "punk as fuck", like a squat with legal electricity. The move to Philadelphia's Relapse Records put the band next to metal and doom acts rather than the noise-rock crowd.

Austin has said the song "Pinnacle" was written in a depressed stretch after a close friend's betrayal. Decibel put the album in its Hall of Fame in 2017.

years.h: Hydra Head 7-inch In These Black Days covers Black Sabbath
years.p: The 7-inch includes a version of "Sabbath Bloody Sabbath."

eras.title: Two Rochester players, one fast record
eras.text: Austin moves to Massachusetts, then rebuilds around drummer Brann Dailor and bassist Bill Kelliher from Lethargy. The result is In the Eyes of God, and the seed of Mastodon.

years.cap: Today Is the Day live, ca. 1999
years.h: Austin moves to Massachusetts and takes his studio with him
years.p: After relocating in 1998, [[Steve Austin|bf1e2347-b742-452e-88e9-320b0d23acad]] set up Austin Enterprise in Clinton, Massachusetts; most Today Is the Day albums since were made there. Wikipedia notes Elrod also played a short stint that year.

yt: Brann Dailor on his career before Mastodon and Today Is the Day
years.h: Two future Mastodon members play on In the Eyes of God
years.p: Brann Dailor and Bill Kelliher are the only lineup of Today Is the Day on this record; both went on to found [[Mastodon|bc5e2ad6-0a4a-4d90-b911-e9a7e6861727]]. Austin wrote the title song in response to the 1993 Waco siege.
years.xp:
The first pressing was 1,000 copies: 900 for sale and 100 clear-vinyl copies for Relapse staff. Terrorizer ranked it ninth in its 1999 albums of the year.

Austin told Revolver he wanted the fastest and most technical Today Is the Day record, and that it was recorded three times. Dailor and Kelliher had come from Rochester's [[Lethargy|16e540ae-cff3-4b47-8ebe-96b18caa396e]].

years.h: Live Till You Die pulls from two tours, with covers
years.p: Live tracks from the Temple of the Morning Star and In the Eyes of God tours, plus covers, on Relapse.

years.cap: Today Is the Day on stage, ca. 1999
years.h: Dailor and Kelliher leave after one album; Chris Debari joins
years.p: The Kelliher-Dailor lineup ends after In the Eyes of God, and [[Chris Debari|061a05fa-01a9-4112-b391-5105d0ab2939]] joins on bass.

eras.title: Bigger records, then a label of his own
eras.text: With Chris Debari on bass the band puts out a two-and-a-half-hour double album, leaves Relapse and releases records on Austin's own SuperNova.

years.h: Sadness Will Prevail runs two and a half hours over two discs
years.p: Three years of writing and six months to record at Austin Enterprise. Guests include Seth Putnam on vocals and Kris Force on violin.
years.xp:
Austin said the two-disc idea followed earlier records that were fast and stripped down, and that being snowed in with his family helped. Each track is mixed to flow into the next like a film score.

Reviews split: AllMusic complained about the low-end mix and filler; Maelstrom Zine called it the band's most complete effort.

years.cap: Kiss the Pig cover art by Takanami Kazuhiko
years.h: Slayer in Japan leads to Kiss the Pig
years.p: Austin wrote most of it after playing Japan with Slayer, and met the charcoal artist Takanami Kazuhiko, whose painting became the cover. It was the last album on Relapse.
years.xp: The 36-minute record was cut between November 2003 and April 2004 in Nashville and Clinton. Austin has called the song "This Machine Kills Fascists" a response to police militarization and unrest.

years.h: SuperNova Records starts up
years.p: [[Steve Austin|bf1e2347-b742-452e-88e9-320b0d23acad]] launches the label to reissue the band's out-of-print albums.

years.cap: Steve Austin at Die By The Wolf Fest, Init, June 2008
years.h: Axis of Eden arrives with its own film
years.p: Released on SuperNova, it is the only Today Is the Day album with drummer [[Derek Roddy|8ba019fc-74fd-4e8c-9537-32fbeb3d6d3e]] and the last with Chris Debari. A film by David Hall premiered on tour day one.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says "Broken Promises and Dead Dreams" was written as commentary on Relapse Records, and "Free at Last" grew from a piano piece after an argument between Austin and his wife.

The film played behind the band on the tour. A digital release of it followed in 2008.

eras.title: Second wind on the road
eras.text: New labels, a Converge guitarist at the board, a van that rolled and burned, and a long recovery. Austin keeps going.

years.h: Today Is the Day plays AmRep's 25th birthday in Minneapolis
years.p: Today Is the Day played [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s Amphetamine Reptile 25th-anniversary weekend, on a bill with the Melvins and Boss Hog.

years.h: Kurt Ballou records Pain Is a Warning in Salem
years.p: Recorded at Godcity Studio in Salem, Mass. for Black Market Activities, with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] of Converge playing guitar on "This Is You."
years.xp: Austin took the title from his young son, who said it after watching Shutter Island. Themes include the 2008 financial crisis and his mother's Alzheimer's.

years.cap: Steve Austin at Pumpehuset, Copenhagen, November 23, 2015
years.h: A tour van rolls and burns the year Animal Mother comes out
years.p: Made in Orland, Maine, as Austin's mother declined; it came out on Southern Lord Records. A tour van accident that year broke his ribs.
years.xp: Austin told Revolver the van rolled at 65 miles per hour and burned. He later had a shattered hip socket that took years to be diagnosed, and Lyme disease.

years.h: Austin and Unsane's Chris Spencer start UXO
years.p: Austin formed the side project UXO with [[Unsane|db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b]]'s Chris Spencer; the self-titled album came out on Reptilian Records.

years.h: Jef Whitehead of Leviathan paints the cover of No Good to Anyone
years.p: Work began in 2016 and slowed with Austin's health, so it was the band's longest gap between records. BMG released it.
years.xp: A US tour with 16, Child Bite and The Obsessed was cut short by COVID-19. The album has a song for Austin's dog Callie, who died of Lyme disease.

eras.title: The catalog comes home
eras.text: Steve Austin takes back his masters, releases a new album and loses the band's first bassist.

years.h: Austin takes back the masters
years.p: He holds the rights to the whole catalog and reactivates SuperNova Records to reissue the albums.

years.h: Mike Herrell, the band's first bassist, dies
years.p: The band posted that its founding bassist Mike Herrell had died and called him one of the greatest bass players of all time. Sources found give no cause.

years.h: Never Give In goes from industrial grind to horns
years.p: On SuperNova. Angry Metal Guy hears industrial grind, horn arrangements and Americana, and cites Austin's loss and homelessness.
